claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a fine lamellar microstructure consisting of coupled FCC and B2 phases.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits high strength and ductility at room temperature.
Aging at approximately 400–600 °C is an intermediate regime in which classical grain-boundary embrittlement is absent.
Intermediate aging enhances local chemical order and chemical short-range order within coherent B2 domains.
Intermediate aging changes phase-boundary morphology by producing or retaining coherent B2 interfaces.
Chemical short-range order reduces screw-dislocation mobility in the B2 domains.
Enhanced chemical short-range order promotes cross-slip locking of screw dislocations.
Cross-slip locking of screw dislocations can provide additional strengthening.
Reduced dislocation mobility and cross-slip locking cause the intermediate-temperature loss of ductility.
Higher-temperature aging causes the B2 domains to coarsen or lose coherency.
The influence of short-range order on screw-dislocation motion decreases as temperature increases.
B2 coarsening or loss of coherency reduces short-range-order resistance and restores dislocation mobility.
Higher-temperature aging restores ductility after the intermediate-temperature brittle regime.
The ductile-brittle-ductile transition occurs without significant grain growth or impurity segregation at grain boundaries.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism operates in grain interiors through dislocation-order interactions rather than through grain-boundary impurity segregation.
The embrittlement regime begins where B2 ordering is maximized while the domains remain coherent and ends when the domains begin to coarsen or lose coherency.
If grain-boundary embrittlement is dominant, the loss of ductility should correlate with impurity segregation at grain boundaries rather than with local chemical-order evolution.
